titulo: Review and test of the first block: The most common mistakes

aula.titulo: Review and test of the first block
aula.objetivo: Review pronunciation, articles, the present, the accusative, separable verbs, time and directions, fix the most common English-speaker mistakes, and take the test for the first block.

blocos.explicacao: These ten mistakes show up most often in English speakers. Fixing just these makes your German sound far more natural. Read each pair out loud: first the wrong one (to recognize how odd it sounds), then the right one.

erros.motivo: Same as English: "I am 20 years old" — but don't drop alt after Jahre.
No "do": the verb itself opens the question.
No "am …-ing": one verb form covers both.
One "the" in English, three in German: learn the article with the word.
Capital letter at the start and on every noun; languages too, as in English.
The second verb goes to the end.
A masculine thing is ihn, not "it" = es.
The separable prefix goes to the very end, not where English puts "off".
halb looks ahead: half an hour BEFORE three (British "half three" is the opposite).

itens.ru: Wie heißt du? / Wie heißen Sie?
itens.audio: Wie heißt du? / Wie heißen Sie?

itens.pt: How do you say … in German?

itens.explicacao: Wo asks where someone lives: Wo wohnst du? Wohin asks about a destination and woher about origin.

itens.enunciado: Ask about the destination: ___ gehst du heute?
itens.explicacao: We need the destination. Wohin means "where to": Wohin gehst du heute? (Where are you going today?)

itens.enunciado: Ask about the origin: ___ kommt Tom?
itens.explicacao: We need the origin. Woher means "where from": Woher kommt Tom? Wohin would ask about a destination.
The answer is a person, so use wer ("who"): Wer ist das?
To ask about an activity, use was ("what"): Was machst du heute? Wer asks about a person, not an action.

itens.enunciado: Which of the three is a yes/no question?
itens.explicacao: Wohnst du hier? is a yes/no question: the conjugated verb comes before the subject. The other options start with question words and ask for specific information.

itens.enunciado: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: ___ du Deutsch? (lernen) · Wo wohnt Camila? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: With du, lernen becomes lernst. In a yes/no question, the conjugated verb opens the sentence: Lernst du Deutsch?

itens.enunciado: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: Lernst du Deutsch? (lernen) · Wo ___ Camila? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: Camila is third person singular; wohnen becomes wohnt. In a question with Wo, the verb comes right after the question word: Wo wohnt Camila?

itens.enunciado: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: Woher ___ ihr? (kommen) · Wohnen Sie in München? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: With ihr, kommen becomes kommt. After Woher, it's verb then subject: Woher kommt ihr?

itens.enunciado: Complete the questions by conjugating the verb: Woher kommt ihr? (kommen) · ___ Sie in München? (wohnen)
itens.explicacao: With formal Sie, wohnen stays wohnen. A yes/no question starts with the verb: Wohnen Sie in München?

itens.enunciado: Turn it into a yes/no question, in the order verb–subject–time: Tom arbeitet heute. → ___
itens.explicacao: Put the conjugated verb before the subject and keep heute at the end: Arbeitet Tom heute? — no "does" needed.

itens.enunciado: Match each question to the right answer: (1) Wer ist das? · (2) Was machst du? · (3) Wie alt bist du? · (4) Woher kommst du? · (5) Wo wohnst du? Answers: (a) In Schwabing. · (b) Ich bin 28 Jahre alt. · (c) Das ist Jonas. · (d) Aus Brasilien. · (e) Ich lerne Deutsch.

blocos.enunciado: Read each mistake out loud and say the correct form. Then record 5 sentences of your own without any of these mistakes.
Write 3 mistakes you've made in German and the correct form.
